# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **State**: open

- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

AGENTS.md
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# gh-710: conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa #1211, 2026-10-04)

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted 5 new threads. Result: pr_approved + ai_validated + unresolved threads = mergeStateStatus BLOCKED (conversation gate), while the rework-arm rules never fire because the latest verdict is APPROVE, not REQUEST_CHANGES. The PR deadlocked until a manual rework dispatch.

## Fix

The rework-unresolved-threads rule must arm agent:rework on unresolved review threads regardless of the latest verdict being APPROVE (or the merge rule must tolerate suggestion-only threads — less safe). Suggestion: gate on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review in flight.

## Evidence

fa #1211: 5 threads from the 14:13 APPROVE re-review blocked merge ~1h; resolved only after manual ai-teammate pr=1211 leg=rework dispatch.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Still no window for rule 22 (ai_validating present continuously except within-tick gaps between rule 4 unarm and rule 7 re-arm — rule 22 runs after 7). Confirmed.

Also check: is there any OTHER existing rule that consumes ai_validating for BLOCKED+green? validated-green excludes pr_approved. unarm-stale-validation only BEHIND. merge-validated only CLEAN. No. Confirmed the spin.

Also potential IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION findings:

1. **Comment text inaccuracy** (already noted in PR description as cosmetic): arm_rework comment says "once the threads are resolved a fresh re-review is armed (review-threads-resolved)" — for approved PRs, review-threads-resolved excludes pr_approved, so NO re-review is armed; re-validation + merge follows. The PR description acknowledges this ("cosmetic only, left unchanged"). It's misleading in exactly the scenario this PR fixes — operators reading the comment on an approved PR will expect a re-review that never comes. I'd rate IMPORTANT (comment actively misdescribes the machine path for the gh-710 case). smAgent.js line ~1146 comment is in the diff? No — the diff only touches sm_github.json description + tests. The comment is in js/smAgent.js, unchanged. Not in the diff → goes to general comment per rules. Hmm, actually the arm_rework comment lives in smAgent.js which is NOT in the PR diff. So inline comment not possible; mention in general.

2. **Test duplication**: the new gh-710 test in test_smAgent.js re-checks in-flight guards already checked in the gh-683 hygiene test directly above (the modified assertion). Slight redundancy; fine as regression pinning. SUGGESTION-level, borderline not worth flagging... The gh-683 test now checks the 4 remaining guards; the gh-710 test checks them again. It's intentional pinning. I'd skip or make it a SUGGESTION.

3. **Description length**: the sm_github.json description is now enormous (~2.5KB single line). Pre-existing pattern though. Not flagging.

4. The test in test_smGithubSource.js: the `load(...)` mock signature — they added a 5th arg? Let me verify the test passes — full suite passed 1507, so yes.

5. Also verify the disjointness claim in the description: "review-stale-verdict ... now excludes agent:rework" — checked in tests. And review-stale-verdict has no threads guard and excludes pr_approved — so an approved PR with unresolved threads doesn't match it. Good.

6. One more: could rework-unresolved-threads now fire on a PR with pr_approved + unresolved threads while a VALIDATION is genuinely needed... no — validation is needed only for merge; merge is BLOCKED by threads anyway.

7. What about `validate-fresh` / `review-machine-unlinked` etc.? review-machine-unlinked: labels [ai_validated], notLabels [ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved, agent:review, ai_validating] — pr_approved excluded. Fine.

8. Consider double-arming: rework-unresolved-threads arms agent:rework while PR is pr_approved. rework-on-label dispatches the rework leg — does the rework leg work on approved PRs? pushReworkChanges handles stickyApproved (commented "re-review NOT armed; re-validation + merge follow"). Good.

9. But: after rework finishes on an approved PR — it resolves threads, pushes new head. New head → validate-armed: ai_validated latch is on old head, latch-skip probe requires head SHA == green validation SHA → head moved → latch-skip no match → real dispatch. Good, re-validation happens. But wait: does rework push even when the only change is thread resolution (no code change)? headMovedSinceLastReview... For stickyApproved it doesn't matter; validation re-runs on same head via latch-skip arm (head unchanged → latch-skip arm without dispatch, merge proceeds). Good.

10. CI status: no ci_failures.md input → no CI failures to flag. Machine jobs show dev run done ✅. PR description says full suite 1484 passed; I ran the suite: 1507 passed, 0 failed. Good.

11. Test count mismatch: description says 1484; actual run now 1507 (includes PR's own +2 tests and possibly others merged since). Not an issue.

Now let me also verify there is no `pr_files.txt` — correct, absent. And no ci_failures/discussions files. Fine.

Let me also double check the claim in the rework rule description about "review-stale-verdict (the one armer without a threads guard) now excludes agent:rework" — verified in the python dump: review-stale-verdict notLabels [agent:review, agent:rework, ai_validating, pr_approved]. ✓.

And the disjointness: review-threads-resolved threadsResolved true; rework rule false. ✓ One PR can't arm both. ✓.

The natural anchor: sm_github.json line where `pr_approved` was removed from notLabels (the `-              "pr_approved",` line — a removed line, side LEFT) or the rework rule's query context. GitHub review threads can attach to removed lines too (side LEFT). Alternatively anchor on the description line (RIGHT 486). I'll anchor on the removed "pr_approved" line with side LEFT... The instructions say inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff; removed lines are present in the diff (as `-` lines). Typically acceptable with side LEFT. Let me get exact line numbers from the diff.

From the git diff: hunk `@@ -494,7 +494,6 @@` — the removed line `"pr_approved",` is at old line 497 (494 + 3 context + ...). Let me compute: hunk starts old 494: lines 494 `"agent:rework",`, 495 `"agent:review",`, 496 `"ai_validating",`, 497 `-"pr_approved",`, 498 `"validation_failed"`. So old-side line 497. New-side: 494,495,496,497(validation_failed). For side LEFT, line=497.

Also the IMPORTANT finding about the arm_rework comment — in js/smAgent.js, not in diff → general comment only.

Wait — I should also reconsider: is my BLOCKING analysis airtight? One thing to verify: within a tick, do rules really see labels written by earlier rules in the same tick? The fail-validation description explicitly documents: "the unarm below frees the limit-1 mutex and (with the openPrs ioCache drop in the action) the arm rule's later query in the SAME tick sees the freed slot and arms the NEXT oldest approved" — yes, confirmed for the unarm path. For label ADDITION visibility: the latch-skip arm at rule 7 adds ai_validating; rule 22's query re-runs github_list_prs... does rule 22's query use the cached open-PR list (per-tick ioCache) that would NOT include the just-added label? Hmm! "the openPrs ioCache drop in the action" — the unarm action DROPS the cache so later queries re-fetch. Does github_add_labels (used by validate_pr latch-skip arm) drop the cache? If NOT, rule 22 might query a STALE list without ai_validating and MATCH — which would actually make the fix work!

Let me check smAgent.js for ioCache handling around label add/remove.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# gh-710: conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa #1211, 2026-10-04)

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted 5 new threads. Result: pr_approved + ai_validated + unresolved threads = mergeStateStatus BLOCKED (conversation gate), while the rework-arm rules never fire because the latest verdict is APPROVE, not REQUEST_CHANGES. The PR deadlocked until a manual rework dispatch.

## Fix

The rework-unresolved-threads rule must arm agent:rework on unresolved review threads regardless of the latest verdict being APPROVE (or the merge rule must tolerate suggestion-only threads — less safe). Suggestion: gate on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review in flight.

## Evidence

fa #1211: 5 threads from the 14:13 APPROVE re-review blocked merge ~1h; resolved only after manual ai-teammate pr=1211 leg=rework dispatch.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**
