# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

AGENTS.md
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Removing `pr_approved` here is the right change, and I verified the happy path end-to-end: on the approval tick, `validate-armed` (rule index 7) matches the now-deadlocked PR (`BLOCKED` passes its `notMergeState: [BEHIND, DIRTY]` guard, mutex free) and arms `ai_validating`; `rework-unresolved-threads` (index 22) then matches in the same tick and arms `agent:rework`; `rework-on-label` dispatches the leg; the sticky-approval path in `pushReworkChanges.js` resolves the threads (gh-692 sweep), pushes, skips re-review, and `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches CI on the new head → `merge-validated` merges. It converges.

**The fragility**: rule 22 only matches in that tick because `validate_pr`'s label-add (`js/smAgent.js`, latch-skip arm ~line 1599 and post-dispatch arm ~line 1717) does **not** call `dropOpenPrsCache`. Rule 22 re-queries via `listOpenPrs()`, which hits the per-tick ioCache entry populated earlier in the tick (e.g. by `merge-validated`'s query) — a snapshot *without* the just-added `ai_validating` — so the exclusion never sees the arm. That directly contradicts the stated owner directive of 2026-10-04 (`smAgent.js` line ~3076: *"Invalidate-after-mutation: PR labels changed mid-tick — a later rule re-querying the open-PR list in the SAME tick must see it"*), which was implemented on all three **unarm** paths (lines 1748, 2247, 2549) but not the **arm** paths. The moment someone completes the directive by adding `dropOpenPrsCache` to the validate_pr arms — a natural, review-approved "fix" — this rule stops matching the sole-approved-PR case and gh-710 silently regresses: the PR spins forever in a `validate-armed` (latch-skip arm) ↔ `sweep-stale-validating` (15-min unarm, cache dropped, re-fetched and re-cached *pre-arm* by validate-armed itself) loop, `ai_validating` is present at rule-22 evaluation time every tick, rework never fires. None of the new tests catch this: they pin config shape and source-query matching, not the tick-level ordering.

**Suggestions to make it robust** (any one):
1. Add `agent:rework` to `validate-armed`'s `notLabels` and move `rework-unresolved-threads` before it in the rule list (rework arms first on the approval tick; validation defers until the leg consumes the label and pushes). Needs the gh-683 ORDER test adjusted, and the re-review armers' stacking guarantees re-checked.
2. Or gate `validate-armed` with `threadsResolved: true` — arming validation for a PR whose merge is conversation-BLOCKED is wasted work anyway. Caveat: think through guest-authored approved PRs with open threads (the rework rule is machine-only by design, so no leg would ever own their threads).
3. Or, minimum: pin the current same-tick visibility with an explicit comment at the validate_pr arm sites ("do NOT dropOpenPrsCache here — rework-unresolved-threads relies on seeing pre-arm labels, gh-710") plus a hygiene test, so the accidental behavior becomes contractual.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

It converges.

**The fragility**: rule 22 only matches in that tick because `validate_pr`'s label-add (`js/smAgent.js`, latch-skip arm ~line 1599 and post-dispatch arm ~line 1717) does **not** call `dropOpenPrsCache`. Rule 22 re-queries via `listOpenPrs()`, which hits the per-tick ioCache entry populated earlier in the tick (e.g. by `merge-validated`'s query) — a snapshot *without* the just-added `ai_validating` — so the exclusion never sees the arm. That directly contradicts the stated owner directive of 2026-10-04 (`smAgent.js` line ~3076: *"Invalidate-after-mutation: PR labels changed mid-tick — a later rule re-querying the open-PR list in the SAME tick must see it"*), which was implemented on all three **unarm** paths (lines 1748, 2247, 2549) but not the **arm** paths. The moment someone completes the directive by adding `dropOpenPrsCache` to the validate_pr arms — a natural, review-approved "fix" — this rule stops matching the sole-approved-PR case and gh-710 silently regresses: the PR spins forever in a `validate-armed` (latch-skip arm) ↔ `sweep-stale-validating` (15-min unarm, cache dropped, re-fetched and re-cached *pre-arm* by validate-armed itself) loop, `ai_validating` is present at rule-22 evaluation time every tick, rework never fires. None of the new tests catch this: they pin config shape and source-query matching, not the tick-level ordering.

1. Add `agent:rework` to `validate-armed`'s `notLabels` and move `rework-unresolved-threads` before it in the rule list (rework arms first on the approval tick; validation defers until the leg consumes the label and pushes). Needs the gh-683 ORDER test adjusted, and the re-review armers' stacking guarantees re-checked.
2. Or gate `validate-armed` with `threadsResolved: true` — arming validation for a PR whose merge is conversation-BLOCKED is wasted work anyway. Caveat: think through guest-authored approved PRs with open threads (the rework rule is machine-only by design, so no leg would ever own their threads).
3. Or, minimum: pin the current same-tick visibility with an explicit comment at the validate_pr arm sites ("do NOT dropOpenPrsCache here — rework-unresolved-threads relies on seeing pre-arm labels, gh-710") plus a hygiene test, so the accidental behavior becomes contractual.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/718
- **Title**: gh-710 conveyor gap: rework arm never fires on APPROVE-with-unresolved-threads (merge deadlock)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-710` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +56
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:37:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Re-review verdict was APPROVE but posted new unresolved threads → `pr_approved` + `ai_validated` + unresolved threads = `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (conversation gate). The `rework-unresolved-threads` rule (`sm_github.json`) listed `pr_approved` in `notLabels`, so the rework arm never fired on the exact PR that needed it; red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Merge blocked + no armed leg = deadlock until a manual rework dispatch (live: fa #1211, ~1h).

### Fix

- `sm_github.json` — `rework-unresolved-threads` rule: removed `pr_approved` from `query.notLabels`. The rule now gates on unresolved-thread count > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation in flight (remaining `notLabels`: `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `ai_validating`, `validation_failed`) — per the ticket's suggested gating, the safer option. Sticky approval makes rework the correct leg: after the rework push, `validate-armed` re-validates and merge proceeds without a re-review. Rule description updated with the gh-710 rationale.

### Test Coverage

- RED: new `rework-unresolved-threads: gh-710` hygiene test failed against the old config (`pr_approved` in `notLabels` at index 3) before the fix.
- `test_smAgent.js` — gh-710 regression test (config shape: `pr_approved` not excluded, in-flight guards kept, `review-threads-resolved` still excludes `pr_approved`); gh-683 test updated to the new shape.
- `test_smGithubSource.js` — gh-683 matching test now covers the live fa #1211 shape: `pr_approved` + 5 unresolved threads matches; resolved/threadless/guest/validating still don't.
- Full suite: **1484 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- Disjointness preserved: `review-threads-resolved` / `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` require `threadsResolved: true` (this rule is the false side) — one PR can never arm both legs.
- `mergeBot` is unaffected: a BLOCKED approved PR is logged as FIFO-queued and never merged while threads are open; once the rework leg resolves threads and pushes, the normal validate→merge path resumes.
- The `arm_rework` comment text mentions a fresh re-review after threads resolve; for approved PRs the actual path is re-validation + merge (no re-review) — cosmetic only, left unchanged to keep the fix minimal.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the fix works today only by an undocumented cache-staleness accident — make the validate-armed interplay explicit**

Removing `pr_approved` here is the right change, and I verified the happy path end-to-end: on the approval tick, `validate-armed` (rule index 7) matches the now-deadlocked PR (`BLOCKED` passes its `notMergeState: [BEHIND, DIRTY]` guard, mutex free) and arms `ai_validating`; `rework-unresolved-threads` (index 22) then matches in the same tick and arms `agent:rework`; `rework-on-label` dispatches the leg; the sticky-approval path in `pushReworkChanges.js` resolves the threads (gh-692 sweep), pushes, skips re-review, and `revalidate-armed` re-dispatches CI on the new head → `merge-validated` merges. It converges.

**The fragility**: rule 22 only matches in that tick because `validate_pr`'s label-add (`js/smAgent.js`, latch-skip arm ~line 1599 and post-dispatch arm ~line 1717) does **not** call `dropOpenPrsCache`. Rule 22 re-queries via `listOpenPrs()`, which hits the per-tick ioCache entry populated earlier in the tick (e.g. by `merge-validated`'s query) — a snapshot *without* the just-added `ai_validating` — so the exclusion never sees the arm. That directly contradicts the stated owner directive of 2026-10-04 (`smAgent.js` line ~3076: *"Invalidate-after-mutation: PR labels changed mid-tick — a later rule re-querying the open-PR list in the SAME tick must see it"*), which was implemented on all three **unarm** paths (lines 1748, 2247, 2549) but not the **arm** paths. The moment someone completes the directive by adding `dropOpenPrsCache` to the validate_pr arms — a natural, review-approved "fix" — this rule stops matching the sole-approved-PR case and gh-710 silently regresses: the PR spins forever in a `validate-armed` (latch-skip arm) ↔ `sweep-stale-validating` (15-min unarm, cache dropped, re-fetched and re-cached *pre-arm* by validate-armed itself) loop, `ai_validating` is present at rule-22 evaluation time every tick, rework never fires. None of the new tests catch this: they pin config shape and source-query matching, not the tick-level ordering.

**Suggestions to make it robust** (any one):
1. Add `agent:rework` to `validate-armed`'s `notLabels` and move `rework-unresolved-threads` before it in the rule list (rework arms first on the approval tick; validation defers until the leg consumes the label and pushes). Needs the gh-683 ORDER test adjusted, and the re-review armers' stacking guarantees re-checked.
2. Or gate `validate-armed` with `threadsResolved: true` — arming validation for a PR whose merge is conversation-BLOCKED is wasted work anyway. Caveat: think through guest-authored approved PRs with open threads (the rework rule is machine-only by design, so no leg would ever own their threads).
3. Or, minimum: pin the current same-tick visibility with an explicit comment at the validate_pr arm sites ("do NOT dropOpenPrsCache here — rework-unresolved-threads relies on seeing pre-arm labels, gh-710") plus a hygiene test, so the accidental behavior becomes contractual.

## Verdict: APPROVE (0 blocking · 1 important · 1 suggestion)

**What I verified:**
- **Ticket ACs satisfied** — the ticket asked to gate `rework-unresolved-threads` on "unresolved threads > 0 AND no active rework/review in flight, regardless of APPROVE verdict"; the PR implements exactly that by dropping only `pr_approved` from `notLabels` (the other four in-flight guards stay).
- **Fix correctness traced end-to-end** — on the approval tick, `validate-armed` arms `ai_validating`, rule 22 arms `agent:rework`, `rework-on-label` dispatches, the sticky-approval path in `pushReworkChanges.js` (gh-692 thread-resolution sweep, no re-review) closes the loop into re-validate → merge. Disjointness vs the `threadsResolved: true` re-review armers preserved.
- **Tests** — no `ci_failures.md` in the job input; I ran the full suite locally: **1507 passed, 0 failed** (supersedes the PR's claimed 1484).

**Findings:**
1. **⚠️ IMPORTANT (inline, `sm_github.json` LEFT line 497)** — the fix's firing in the sole-approved-PR case rests on an undocumented accident: `validate_pr`'s label-add is the *only* mid-tick mutation path that does **not** call `dropOpenPrsCache`, so rule 22 sees pre-arm labels from the stale per-tick ioCache. This contradicts the owner's 2026-10-04 invalidate-after-mutation directive ("a later rule re-querying the open-PR list in the SAME tick must see it") — implemented on all three unarm paths but not the arm paths. Extending the directive to the arms would silently re-break gh-710 with all tests green (nothing pins the tick-level interplay). Offered three robustness options.
2. **⚠️ IMPORTANT (general only — file not in diff)** — the `arm_rework` comment in `js/smAgent.js` (~line 1146) promises "a fresh re-review is armed (review-threads-resolved)", which is false for approved PRs (that rule excludes `pr_approved`). Harmless before this PR (the rule never fired on approved PRs); now it will mislead on every gh-710-shaped PR.
3. **💡 SUGGESTION (inline, `test_smAgent.js:803`)** — the new gh-710 test duplicates the four-guard assertion already updated in the gh-683 hygiene test above.
